Ashes of the Ninth Sky

Chapter 7 - The Bell Below the Lake

Previous
Chapter Next
Chapter

The bell rang again at midnight, though the lake had been frozen solid for a week and no boat could have reached the drowned chapel beneath it.

Mara pressed her palm flat against the ice. The vibration came up through her bones, slow and patient, like a giant knocking politely at a door it already knew would open.

“We should go back,” whispered Fen. His breath hung in the air between them. “Whatever that is, it isn’t calling for us.”

“Then who is it calling for?” Mara asked, and when he had no answer she began to cut.

The ice was thicker than she expected. Her hatchet bit and slipped, bit and slipped, throwing up chips that glittered in the lantern light like scattered teeth. After an hour her shoulders burned and the hole was barely wide enough for a hand.

Below, in the black water, something gold turned slowly over and was gone.

Fen swore under his breath and took the hatchet from her without a word. They worked in turns after that, trading the blade back and forth until the moon slid down behind the pines and the bell, at last, fell silent.
